speaker: Doctor
text:
Let me start by asking: Can you describe the appearance of the rash? Is it raised, scaly, or just flat and red?

Please tell me how long you have been experiencing this and if there are any other symptoms like fever or joint pain.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient complains of a pruritic rash on both upper extremities that has been present for 5 months. She notes that the rash occasionally worsens but has not completely resolved at any point. She denies any recent illnesses and mentions that she has not started any new medications or come into contact with any new substances that she is aware of.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is helpful; the chronic nature of this rash makes me suspect a dermatological condition like psoriasis or eczema rather than an acute infection. Have you noticed any scaling, silvery patches, or fissures on the rash, and do the symptoms worsen after taking a hot shower or with stress?

REQUEST TEST: Tzanck_Pap Smear, Skin_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin_Biopsy: Intraepidermal accumulation of edematous fluid and widening of intercellular spaces between keratinocytes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pruritic rash on the bilateral upper extremities. I also have No fever, No joint pains, No recent illnesses. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous diagnosis of a urinary tract infection does not match your presentation of a chronic, pruritic rash on your arms; UTIs typically cause urinary symptoms rather than skin lesions. While I requested a skin biopsy earlier, I need to clarify if you have any personal or family history of atopic dermatitis or psoriasis, and please confirm if the rash has any silvery scale or appears in a specific pattern like knuckles or elbows.

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Clinical_Photographs

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No history of serious illness. No known drug allergies. Takes no medications. Social history: College student studying graphic design. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your background in graphic design and the chronic nature of this rash, could you describe exactly which areas of your upper extremities are affected, and does the itching worsen with sweating or heat?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Psoriasis
